# xfo-miner v1.0.5

This release publishes BATCH 63 and promotes the recent Windows miner hotfixes into a formal cross-platform lifecycle baseline.

## Highlights

- Hardened managed subprocess stop behavior on Windows so miner-controlled child processes no longer fail on unsupported `SIGTERM` semantics.
- Added an explicit OTA quiesce contract before handoff so `xmrig`, idle subprocesses, and other managed children are stopped before update execution.
- Introduced a single-instance guard for the miner main process, preventing duplicate miner runtimes from coexisting in the same identity domain.

## BATCH 63 Scope

### MINER_200 — Windows process stop semantics hardening

- `internal/process/manager.go` now uses a Windows-specific terminate path instead of relying on `syscall.SIGTERM`.
- `internal/process/proc.go` now exposes `ManagedProcess.Kill()` so the process owner layer can terminate managed subprocesses without leaking platform logic upward.
- Added regression coverage for Windows stop and stop-all flows to ensure managed process ownership is cleaned up correctly after termination.

### MINER_201 — Cross-platform OTA handoff cleanup and xmrig lifecycle containment

- OTA handoff now explicitly quiesces the runtime through:
  - idle miner stop
  - `xmrig` stop
  - managed subprocess stop-all
- If OTA quiesce fails, updater execution is skipped and the miner restores the expected standby runtime instead of proceeding with a half-contained handoff.
- If updater execution fails after quiesce, standby/full-mode recovery is also restored deterministically.

### MINER_202 — Single-instance guard and OTA coexistence regression coverage

- Startup now acquires a lock derived from `IdentityStatePath()` before scheduler execution begins.
- Duplicate miner startup in the same runtime identity domain is now rejected fail-closed.
- Added regression coverage for both legal OTA handoff models:
  - Unix `Exec(...)` style replacement
  - Windows `StartProcess(...) + old-process exit` style replacement

## Why this release matters

- Addresses the field failure mode where Windows managed subprocess shutdown could abort early with `send SIGTERM ... not supported by windows`.
- Reduces the risk of OTA-triggered residual `xmrig` / subprocess survivors caused by incomplete pre-handoff cleanup.
- Closes the multi-instance coexistence gap that could allow multiple miner owners to run concurrently and each manage their own child process set.

## Operator notes

- This release is intended to become the new miner lifecycle baseline after BATCH 63.
- Operators using OTA should expect cleaner pre-handoff containment and duplicate-start protection, but no new third-party detached process management behavior is introduced in this batch.
